about: Every voiced line of marrow.ink: who speaks it, the exact words shown on the page ("text"), and what the voice is given ("say": the same words with eleven_v3 audio tags). tools/lines.mjs --check voices.json proves "text" matches the ink; tools/directions.py writes this file. Each line has two takes, media/vo/<id>-1.mp3 and -2.mp3; the page plays one at random.

evening.speaker: quaile
evening.text: That's the light gone. Pub, Sam. I'm buying, so it's halves.
evening.say: [sighs, then brightly] That's the light gone. Pub, Sam. I'm buying, so it's halves.

hub-0.speaker: quaile
hub-0.text: Five people to see before seven, and time for four. Where first?
hub-0.say: [brisk] Five people to see before seven, and time for four. [beat] Where first?

hub-3.speaker: quaile
hub-3.text: One more, then the pub. My feet have been judging chutney since nine.
hub-3.say: [tired, wry] One more, then the pub. My feet have been judging chutney since nine.

p1-open.speaker: narrator
p1-open.text: The Steeple Wyke Horticultural Show, the hundred and twelfth. You have been a detective sergeant in this county for nineteen days.
p1-open.say: [warm, wry] The Steeple Wyke Horticultural Show, the hundred and twelfth. [beat] You have been a detective sergeant in this county for nineteen days.

p10-open.speaker: narrator
p10-open.text: Sunday. The marquee is coming down, and the marrows have gone to the pig farm.
p10-open.say: [dry, unhurried] Sunday. The marquee is coming down, and the marrows have gone to the pig farm.

p10a-1.speaker: narrator
p10a-1.text: Men in shorts are folding the marquee. The Pike Cup is in a box marked Village Hall, Do Not Remove.
p10a-1.say: [dry, unhurried] Men in shorts are folding the marquee. The Pike Cup is in a box marked Village Hall, Do Not Remove.

p10b-1.speaker: narrator
p10b-1.text: Margaret has cut one foxglove, and is putting it in a vase on the kitchen table.
p10b-1.say: [dry, unhurried] Margaret has cut one foxglove, and is putting it in a vase on the kitchen table.

p10b-2.speaker: margaret
p10b-2.text: Thank you, Sergeant. You were very thorough. They look nice indoors, as long as nobody drinks the water.
p10b-2.say: [cool, faint smile] Thank you, Sergeant. You were very thorough. They look nice indoors, [dry] as long as nobody drinks the water.

p10b-3.speaker: margaret
p10b-3.text: The vicar called this morning, to see how I was. I didn't offer him anything.
p10b-3.say: [cool, pointed] The vicar called this morning, to see how I was. I didn't offer him anything.

p10c-1.speaker: narrator
p10c-1.text: Quaile has taken her hearing aid out. It is on the dashboard.
p10c-1.say: [dry, unhurried] Quaile has taken her hearing aid out. It is on the dashboard.

p10c-2.speaker: quaile
p10c-2.text: You did well, Sam. For nineteen days.
p10c-2.say: [warm, grudging] You did well, Sam. For nineteen days.

p10c-4.speaker: quaile
p10c-4.text: Hm? Other side, Sam. That one's off.
p10c-4.say: [loudly, cupping an ear] Hm? Other side, Sam. That one's off.

p10c-5.speaker: quaile
p10c-5.text: Next time, look at the vicar first. In my experience it's the vicar a surprising amount of the time.
p10c-5.say: [drily] Next time, look at the vicar first. In my experience it's the vicar a surprising amount of the time.

p10c-6.speaker: quaile
p10c-6.text: We'll have him on the prize fund by Friday. The foxgloves will take longer.
p10c-6.say: [grim, dry] We'll have him on the prize fund by Friday. The foxgloves will take longer.

p10c-7.speaker: quaile
p10c-7.text: Well. Nobody's dead who wasn't dead yesterday.
p10c-7.say: [sighs] Well. Nobody's dead who wasn't dead yesterday.

p10d-1.speaker: narrator
p10d-1.text: The scarecrows are still along the hedge. The straw vicar has gone.
p10d-1.say: [dry, unhurried] The scarecrows are still along the hedge. The straw vicar has gone.

p10d-2.speaker: narrator
p10d-2.text: At the end of the row is a new one: a navy mac, a loose tie, brown city shoes, a small black notebook. Its card says Our Village, D S Adeyemi.
p10d-2.say: [dry, unhurried] At the end of the row is a new one: a navy mac, a loose tie, brown city shoes, a small black notebook. Its card says Our Village, D S Adeyemi.

p10d-3.speaker: quaile
p10d-3.text: Twenty days, and they've made you already. That's quick.
p10d-3.say: [amused, then uneasy] Twenty days, and they've made you already. That's quick.

p10d-5.speaker: narrator
p10d-5.text: The scarecrows are still along the hedge. The straw vicar has moved to the end of the row.
p10d-5.say: [dry, unhurried] The scarecrows are still along the hedge. The straw vicar has moved to the end of the row.

p10d-6.speaker: narrator
p10d-6.text: Nobody entered it. The card on the straw vicar beside it says Best in Show.
p10d-6.say: [very quiet] Nobody entered it. [beat] The card on the straw vicar beside it says Best in Show.

p1a-1.speaker: narrator
p1a-1.text: Bunting, a marquee, a brass band from the next village, and four hundred people who know each other's business.
p1a-1.say: [amused] Bunting, a marquee, a brass band from the next village, and four hundred people who know each other's business.

p1a-2.speaker: narrator
p1a-2.text: Behind the marquee, a church spire. In front of it, a line of scarecrows.
p1a-2.say: [dry, unhurried] Behind the marquee, a church spire. In front of it, a line of scarecrows.

p1b-1.speaker: quaile
p1b-1.text: You came. Good. I'm judging the chutney, and you're holding the spoons.
p1b-1.say: [brisk, pleased] You came. Good. I'm judging the chutney, and you're holding the spoons.

p1b-2.speaker: sam
p1b-2.text: Ma'am, I was told this was a day off.
p1b-2.say: [polite, wary] Ma'am, I was told this was a day off.

p1b-3.speaker: quaile
p1b-3.text: It is. Nobody has ever been murdered over chutney.
p1b-3.say: [cheerfully] It is. [beat] Nobody has ever been murdered over chutney.

p1c-1.speaker: gerald
p1c-1.text: Gerald Pike, chairman. The marrow results are delayed. Would whoever has moved the marrows please put them back.
p1c-1.say: [shouting into a microphone, pompous] Gerald Pike, chairman. The marrow results are delayed. [irritated] Would whoever has moved the marrows please put them back.

p1c-2.speaker: gerald
p1c-2.text: And the vicar's cordial is in the church-hall flasks again. Do not take them home.
p1c-2.say: [shouting into a microphone, stern] And the vicar's cordial is in the church-hall flasks again. Do not take them home.

p1c-3.speaker: narrator
p1c-3.text: He has judged the marrows for thirty-one years. His own marrow has won for nine.
p1c-3.say: [deadpan] He has judged the marrows for thirty-one years. His own marrow has won for nine.

p1d-1.speaker: narrator
p1d-1.text: The scarecrow competition. This year's theme is Our Village: a straw vicar in a yellow jacket, a straw butcher, and a straw man in a panama hat.
p1d-1.say: [dry, unhurried] The scarecrow competition. This year's theme is Our Village: a straw vicar in a yellow jacket, a straw butcher, and a straw man in a panama hat.

p1d-2.speaker: narrator
p1d-2.text: The straw Gerald has a red rosette, and faces the wrong way.
p1d-2.say: [slightly uneasy] The straw Gerald has a red rosette, and faces the wrong way.

p1d-3.speaker: narrator
p1d-3.text: Behind the produce tent, somebody screams. It is a short scream, and then a very English apology.
p1d-3.say: [deadpan] Behind the produce tent, somebody screams. [beat] It is a short scream, and then a very English apology.

p2-open.speaker: narrator
p2-open.text: Gerald Pike is in a deckchair behind the produce tent, with his hat over his face. The woman who screamed is still apologising.
p2-open.say: [low] Gerald Pike is in a deckchair behind the produce tent, with his hat over his face. [dry] The woman who screamed is still apologising.

p2a-1.speaker: narrator
p2a-1.text: Half the show has followed you round the tent. The brass band has not stopped playing.
p2a-1.say: [dry, unhurried] Half the show has followed you round the tent. The brass band has not stopped playing.

p2a-2.speaker: quaile
p2a-2.text: Keep them back, Sam. Use your height.
p2a-2.say: [calm, firm] Keep them back, Sam. Use your height.

p2b-1.speaker: narrator
p2b-1.text: No pulse. His hand is cool. Under the hat his face is calm, as if somebody has just told him his marrow won.
p2b-1.say: [quiet] No pulse. His hand is cool. Under the hat his face is calm, as if somebody has just told him his marrow won.

p2b-2.speaker: quaile
p2b-2.text: Don't move him. Ring it in. Then look at what's on the grass.
p2b-2.say: [quietly, all business] Don't move him. Ring it in. Then look at what's on the grass.

p2c-1.speaker: narrator
p2c-1.text: A blue enamel flask, half full of something pale. A brown label on a string: Church Hall.
p2c-1.say: [dry, unhurried] A blue enamel flask, half full of something pale. A brown label on a string: Church Hall.

p2c-2.speaker: sam
p2c-2.text: He told everybody not to take them home.
p2c-2.say: [thinking aloud] He told everybody not to take them home.

p2c-3.speaker: quaile
p2c-3.text: Then why has he got one?
p2c-3.say: [sharp] Then why has he got one?

p2d-1.speaker: quaile
p2d-1.text: Seventy-two, heavy, red in the face, a hot day. The doctor will say heart.
p2d-1.say: [weary] Seventy-two, heavy, red in the face, a hot day. The doctor will say heart.

p2d-3.speaker: quaile
p2d-3.text: I'll say a man who tells four hundred people not to touch the vicar's flasks doesn't drink from one.
p2d-3.say: [drily, certain] I'll say a man who tells four hundred people not to touch the vicar's flasks doesn't drink from one.

p2d-4.speaker: quaile
p2d-4.text: The prize-giving is at seven, and the whole village will be in one room. We have till then.
p2d-4.say: [brisk] The prize-giving is at seven, and the whole village will be in one room. We have till then.

p3-open.speaker: narrator
p3-open.text: Margaret Pike is in her garden, two fields from the show, deadheading roses. Nobody has told her. You have to.
p3-open.say: [gentle] Margaret Pike is in her garden, two fields from the show, deadheading roses. Nobody has told her. [quiet] You have to.

p3-open-b.speaker: narrator
p3-open-b.text: Margaret Pike is back in her garden, deadheading roses, as if the afternoon were any other.
p3-open-b.say: [slightly unsettled] Margaret Pike is back in her garden, deadheading roses, as if the afternoon were any other.

p3a-1.speaker: sam
p3a-1.text: Mrs Pike, I'm sorry. Your husband has died.
p3a-1.say: [gently, carefully] Mrs Pike, I'm sorry. Your husband has died.

p3a-2.speaker: margaret
p3a-2.say: [flat, after a pause] At the show?

p3a-4.speaker: margaret
p3a-4.text: He'd have wanted to be in front of it.
p3a-4.say: [dry, not unkind] He'd have wanted to be in front of it.

p3a-b1.speaker: margaret
p3a-b1.text: You've been in his study, Sergeant. Did you find what you wanted?
p3a-b1.say: [cool, faintly mocking] You've been in his study, Sergeant. Did you find what you wanted?

p3a-cold.speaker: margaret
p3a-cold.text: Come to count my foxgloves again, Sergeant?
p3a-cold.say: [icy, dry] Come to count my foxgloves again, Sergeant?

p3b-1.speaker: margaret
p3b-1.text: Gerald only drank from the green flask. Elderflower. He made it himself, and nobody else would touch it.
p3b-1.say: [precise] Gerald only drank from the green flask. Elderflower. He made it himself, [dry] and nobody else would touch it.

p3b-2.speaker: margaret
p3b-2.text: He forgot it this morning. He forgot it every morning, and I took it down to him at twelve.
p3b-2.say: [a little weary] He forgot it this morning. He forgot it every morning, and I took it down to him at twelve.

p3b-4.speaker: margaret
p3b-4.text: Not today. I had the roses.
p3b-4.say: [cool] Not today. [beat] I had the roses.

p3c-1.speaker: narrator
p3c-1.text: Red handles, clean blades. She wears them on a cord round her neck.
p3c-1.say: [dry, unhurried] Red handles, clean blades. She wears them on a cord round her neck.

p3c-2.speaker: margaret
p3c-2.text: If you want to know whether I've cut any foxgloves, Sergeant, count them.
p3c-2.say: [cool, challenging] If you want to know whether I've cut any foxgloves, Sergeant, count them.

p3d-1.speaker: narrator
p3d-1.text: Forty-one foxgloves along the back wall. You count them twice. Every stem is standing.
p3d-1.say: [dry, unhurried] Forty-one foxgloves along the back wall. You count them twice. Every stem is standing.

p3d-2.speaker: narrator
p3d-2.text: At the end of the border stands the scarecrow in the panama hat. An hour ago it was at the show.
p3d-2.say: [uneasy, quiet] At the end of the border stands the scarecrow in the panama hat. An hour ago it was at the show.

p3e-1.speaker: margaret
p3e-1.text: That's the vicar's. Clement takes Gerald a cup of his cordial at every show, and Gerald tips it on the nearest roses when Clement has gone.
p3e-1.say: [recognising it, cool] That's the vicar's. Clement takes Gerald a cup of his cordial at every show, [dry] and Gerald tips it on the nearest roses when Clement has gone.

p3e-2.speaker: margaret
p3e-2.text: He must have been thirsty today.
p3e-2.say: [quietly, pointed] He must have been thirsty today.

p4-open.speaker: narrator
p4-open.text: The marrow tent. Forty marrows on trestles, and one woman in a butcher's apron, who has not left.
p4-open.say: [dry, unhurried] The marrow tent. Forty marrows on trestles, and one woman in a butcher's apron, who has not left.

p4a-1.speaker: narrator
p4a-1.text: Gerald's marrow is on the end of the table. This year it has no card.
p4a-1.say: [dry, unhurried] Gerald's marrow is on the end of the table. This year it has no card.

p4a-2.speaker: dilys
p4a-2.text: He judged it himself. Every year. Nobody said anything, because it was Gerald.
p4a-2.say: [loud, cheerful] He judged it himself. Every year. Nobody said anything, because it was Gerald.

p4b-1.speaker: dilys
p4b-1.text: Dilys Rudd, Rudd's Butchers. I didn't kill him, love. I was weighing.
p4b-1.say: [laughs] Dilys Rudd, Rudd's Butchers. I didn't kill him, love. [cheerful] I was weighing.

p4b-2.speaker: quaile
p4b-2.text: I'm told he was going to disqualify you this year.
p4b-2.say: [mild, probing] I'm told he was going to disqualify you this year.

p4b-4.speaker: narrator
p4b-4.text: The tannoy is calling her to the scales. You have time for one question.
p4b-4.say: [dry, unhurried] The tannoy is calling her to the scales. You have time for one question.

p4b-warm.speaker: dilys
p4b-warm.text: My favourite policeman. Ask me anything, love. One thing.
p4b-warm.say: [warm, loud] My favourite policeman. Ask me anything, love. [beat] One thing.

p4c-1.speaker: narrator
p4c-1.text: In her apron pocket, a veterinary syringe the size of a cucumber.
p4c-1.say: [dry, unhurried] In her apron pocket, a veterinary syringe the size of a cucumber.

p4c-2.speaker: dilys
p4c-2.text: Water. Two pints a night, straight up the stalk. Every grower in this tent does it. Gerald just never caught anyone else.
p4c-2.say: [unashamed, loud] Water. Two pints a night, straight up the stalk. Every grower in this tent does it. [scornful] Gerald just never caught anyone else.

p4d-1.speaker: narrator
p4d-1.text: Her marrow is weeping water from a hole the size of a pin. So is Gerald's.
p4d-1.say: [dry, unhurried] Her marrow is weeping water from a hole the size of a pin. So is Gerald's.

p4d-3.speaker: dilys
p4d-3.text: Thirty-one years. Write that down, love. Big letters.
p4d-3.say: [delighted, loud] Thirty-one years. Write that down, love. Big letters.

p4d-4.speaker: narrator
p4d-4.text: Her marrow is weeping water from a hole the size of a pin. So is Gerald's, and so is every other marrow on the table.
p4d-4.say: [dry, unhurried] Her marrow is weeping water from a hole the size of a pin. So is Gerald's, and so is every other marrow on the table.

p4f-1.speaker: dilys
p4f-1.text: The vicar. Behind the produce tent, about one. Gerald was waving his little notebook at him.
p4f-1.say: [lowering her voice, enjoying it] The vicar. Behind the produce tent, about one. Gerald was waving his little notebook at him.

p4f-2.speaker: dilys
p4f-2.text: Then they shook hands, and the vicar went and fetched him a drink. Very Christian.
p4f-2.say: [sarcastic] Then they shook hands, and the vicar went and fetched him a drink. Very Christian.

p4f-3.speaker: narrator
p4f-3.text: She goes to the scales without a backward look.
p4f-3.say: [dry, unhurried] She goes to the scales without a backward look.

p5-open.speaker: narrator
p5-open.text: The car park is a field. Toby Pike is in the middle of it, on the phone, in suede loafers.
p5-open.say: [dry, unhurried] The car park is a field. Toby Pike is in the middle of it, on the phone, in suede loafers.

p5a-1.speaker: narrator
p5a-1.text: Range Rovers, a tractor, the brass band's minibus. Somebody has parked across the gate, and it is Toby.
p5a-1.say: [dry, unhurried] Range Rovers, a tractor, the brass band's minibus. Somebody has parked across the gate, and it is Toby.

p5b-1.speaker: toby
p5b-1.text: Sorry, sorry. Clients. Toby Pike, Pike and Lowe, Cirencester. Is it Dad?
p5b-1.say: [distracted, smooth] Sorry, sorry. Clients. Toby Pike, Pike and Lowe, Cirencester. [beat] Is it Dad?

p5b-3.speaker: toby
p5b-3.text: Right. Right. Is there a form for probate, or do I just ring someone?
p5b-3.say: [briefly thrown, then businesslike] Right. Right. Is there a form for probate, or do I just ring someone?

p5b-4.speaker: narrator
p5b-4.text: His phone is already buzzing again. He will give you one answer.
p5b-4.say: [dry, unhurried] His phone is already buzzing again. He will give you one answer.

p5b-cold.speaker: toby
p5b-cold.text: Oh. You. Shall I put the phone down myself this time?
p5b-cold.say: [sarcastic, wary] Oh. You. Shall I put the phone down myself this time?

p5b-warm.speaker: toby
p5b-warm.text: Sergeant! The one who waits. I like a man who waits.
p5b-warm.say: [delighted, smooth] Sergeant! The one who waits. [laughs] I like a man who waits.

p5c-1.speaker: toby
p5c-1.text: In the car, on a call to a man in Swindon from half one till twenty past two. He wants a barn.
p5c-1.say: [glib] In the car, on a call to a man in Swindon from half one till twenty past two. He wants a barn.

p5c-2.speaker: narrator
p5c-2.text: His phone agrees. So does his dashcam, which has filmed him talking to the windscreen for fifty minutes.
p5c-2.say: [dry, unhurried] His phone agrees. So does his dashcam, which has filmed him talking to the windscreen for fifty minutes.

p5c-3.speaker: quaile
p5c-3.text: Your father owned the fields behind the church.
p5c-3.say: [mild] Your father owned the fields behind the church.

p5c-4.speaker: toby
p5c-4.text: Forty houses, if the parish council sees sense. Dad wouldn't. I'm not hiding it.
p5c-4.say: [unembarrassed] Forty houses, if the parish council sees sense. Dad wouldn't. I'm not hiding it.

p5d-1.speaker: narrator
p5d-1.text: There is mud to his ankles and no straw on him anywhere. He has not been near the produce tent.
p5d-1.say: [dry, unhurried] There is mud to his ankles and no straw on him anywhere. He has not been near the produce tent.

p5d-2.speaker: narrator
p5d-2.text: In the back of the brass band's minibus, the straw vicar sits with its seatbelt on.
p5d-2.say: [uneasy, deadpan] In the back of the brass band's minibus, the straw vicar sits with its seatbelt on.

p5e-1.speaker: toby
p5e-1.text: The vicar? Dad said he couldn't add up. Said it twice this week, which for Dad is practically a sermon.
p5e-1.say: [amused] The vicar? Dad said he couldn't add up. Said it twice this week, [laughs] which for Dad is practically a sermon.

p5e-2.speaker: toby
p5e-2.text: Sorry, I have to take this. It's Swindon.
p5e-2.say: [already turning away] Sorry, I have to take this. It's Swindon.

p6-open.speaker: narrator
p6-open.text: St Aldhelm's: the church, the hall, the vicarage, and a roof that has been under scaffolding since Easter.
p6-open.say: [dry, unhurried] St Aldhelm's: the church, the hall, the vicarage, and a roof that has been under scaffolding since Easter.

p6a-1.speaker: clement
p6a-1.text: Sergeant! Inspector! Dreadful. I've been on the cake stall all afternoon, you can ask anyone.
p6a-1.say: [flustered, eager] Sergeant! Inspector! Dreadful. [rushed] I've been on the cake stall all afternoon, you can ask anyone.

p6a-3.speaker: clement
p6a-3.say: [embarrassed laugh] No. Quite. Sorry. [too bright] Cordial?

p6b-1.speaker: narrator
p6b-1.text: The vicarage border: foxgloves, and six of them cut down to the stalk. Clean cuts, this week.
p6b-1.say: [dry, unhurried] The vicarage border: foxgloves, and six of them cut down to the stalk. Clean cuts, this week.

p6c-1.speaker: narrator
p6c-1.text: The church-hall kitchen. Seven hooks, numbered in marker pen. Six blue flasks.
p6c-1.say: [dry, unhurried] The church-hall kitchen. Seven hooks, numbered in marker pen. Six blue flasks.

p6c-2.speaker: clement
p6c-2.text: One always goes walkabout at the show. Gerald's very strict about it. Was.
p6c-2.say: [babbling] One always goes walkabout at the show. Gerald's very strict about it. [catches himself] Was.

p6d-1.speaker: narrator
p6d-1.text: The roof appeal board: a thermometer painted red up to twenty thousand pounds. The target is sixty.
p6d-1.say: [dry, unhurried] The roof appeal board: a thermometer painted red up to twenty thousand pounds. The target is sixty.

p6d-2.speaker: narrator
p6d-2.text: The top of the red is still wet. It has run down over the old paint.
p6d-2.say: [dry, unhurried] The top of the red is still wet. It has run down over the old paint.

p6e-1.speaker: clement
p6e-1.text: Gerald wrote everything down. He once wrote down my sermon. And timed it.
p6e-1.say: [forced laugh] Gerald wrote everything down. He once wrote down my sermon. [nervous] And timed it.

p6e-3.speaker: narrator
p6e-3.text: The vicar puts both hands on his bicycle, as if it might leave without him.
p6e-3.say: [dry, unhurried] The vicar puts both hands on his bicycle, as if it might leave without him.

p7-open.speaker: narrator
p7-open.text: Gerald's study. Margaret lets you in, and stays in the doorway.
p7-open.say: [dry, unhurried] Gerald's study. Margaret lets you in, and stays in the doorway.

p7-open-b.speaker: narrator
p7-open-b.text: Margaret Pike opens the door. Someone has already told her; she does not say who. She lets you into the study and stays in the doorway.
p7-open-b.say: [dry, unhurried] Margaret Pike opens the door. Someone has already told her; she does not say who. She lets you into the study and stays in the doorway.

p7a-1.speaker: narrator
p7a-1.text: Rosettes on every wall, in date order from 1994. Out on the lawn, the scarecrow in the panama hat looks in at the window.
p7a-1.say: [dry, unhurried] Rosettes on every wall, in date order from 1994. Out on the lawn, the scarecrow in the panama hat looks in at the window.

p7a-2.speaker: margaret
p7a-2.text: That wasn't there this morning either.
p7a-2.say: [cool, uneasy] That wasn't there this morning either.

p7b-1.speaker: margaret
p7b-1.text: He kept the Society's books in there. He was treasurer before Clement, and he never forgave him for being better at it.
p7b-1.say: [dry] He kept the Society's books in there. He was treasurer before Clement, and he never forgave him for being better at it.

p7c-1.speaker: narrator
p7c-1.text: A notebook in Gerald's square capitals. Saturday's page: Prize fund four thousand short. Roof? Ask C. After marrows.
p7c-1.say: [dry, unhurried] A notebook in Gerald's square capitals. Saturday's page: Prize fund four thousand short. Roof? Ask C. After marrows.

p7c-2.speaker: sam
p7c-2.text: After the marrows. He was going to ask him today.
p7c-2.say: [realising] After the marrows. He was going to ask him today.

p7c-3.speaker: quaile
p7c-3.text: And he never got past the marrows.
p7c-3.say: [quietly] And he never got past the marrows.

p7c-4.speaker: margaret
p7c-4.text: The vicar came at four, to pray with me. He asked to sit in here on his own for a while.
p7c-4.say: [cool, deliberate] The vicar came at four, to pray with me. He asked to sit in here on his own for a while.

p7c-6.speaker: margaret
p7c-6.text: He looked in the drawers. I suppose that's a kind of prayer.
p7c-6.say: [dry] He looked in the drawers. I suppose that's a kind of prayer.

p7d-1.speaker: narrator
p7d-1.text: Nine silver cups. All of them the Pike Cup, all won by Gerald Pike, all judged by Gerald Pike.
p7d-1.say: [dry, unhurried] Nine silver cups. All of them the Pike Cup, all won by Gerald Pike, all judged by Gerald Pike.

p7d-2.speaker: quaile
p7d-2.text: I'd have poisoned him over that alone.
p7d-2.say: [deadpan] I'd have poisoned him over that alone.

p7d-4.speaker: quaile
p7d-4.text: I'm deaf in one ear, Sam. I can say what I like.
p7d-4.say: [cheerfully] I'm deaf in one ear, Sam. I can say what I like.

p8-open.speaker: narrator
p8-open.text: The Plough, half past six. The whole village is in, and pretending not to listen to you.
p8-open.say: [dry, unhurried] The Plough, half past six. The whole village is in, and pretending not to listen to you.

p8a-1.speaker: narrator
p8a-1.text: The blackboard by the door says Quiz cancelled, mark of respect. Under that, it says Scampi, nine pounds.
p8a-1.say: [dry, unhurried] The blackboard by the door says Quiz cancelled, mark of respect. Under that, it says Scampi, nine pounds.

p8b-1.speaker: quaile
p8b-1.text: Go on, then. Who did it?
p8b-1.say: [mouth half full, amused] Go on, then. Who did it?

p8b-2.speaker: quaile
p8b-2.text: Foxglove's digitalis. On a hot day it stops a big man's heart, and it looks like a big man's heart on a hot day.
p8b-2.say: [matter-of-fact] Foxglove's digitalis. On a hot day it stops a big man's heart, and it looks like a big man's heart on a hot day.

p8b-warm.speaker: quaile
p8b-warm.text: You've learnt to ask me things, Sam. Don't let it go to your head.
p8b-warm.say: [drily, pleased] You've learnt to ask me things, Sam. Don't let it go to your head.

p8c-alibi.speaker: narrator
p8c-alibi.text: Toby, on the phone in a field for fifty minutes.
p8c-alibi.say: [dry, unhurried] Toby, on the phone in a field for fifty minutes.

p8c-argument.speaker: narrator
p8c-argument.text: Gerald and the vicar, behind the produce tent at one. A notebook, a handshake, a drink.
p8c-argument.say: [dry, unhurried] Gerald and the vicar, behind the produce tent at one. A notebook, a handshake, a drink.

p8c-empty.speaker: narrator
p8c-empty.text: Your notebook has the date in it, and the word chutney.
p8c-empty.say: [dry, unhurried] Your notebook has the date in it, and the word chutney.

p8c-flask.speaker: narrator
p8c-flask.text: A church-hall flask by his chair, and he never drank from them.
p8c-flask.say: [dry, unhurried] A church-hall flask by his chair, and he never drank from them.

p8c-foxglove.speaker: narrator
p8c-foxglove.text: Six foxgloves cut at the vicarage. None cut at the Pikes'.
p8c-foxglove.say: [dry, unhurried] Six foxgloves cut at the vicarage. None cut at the Pikes'.

p8c-green.speaker: narrator
p8c-green.text: His own green flask was at home on the draining board.
p8c-green.say: [dry, unhurried] His own green flask was at home on the draining board.

p8c-notebook.speaker: narrator
p8c-notebook.text: Four thousand pounds short in the prize fund. Ask C.
p8c-notebook.say: [dry, unhurried] Four thousand pounds short in the prize fund. Ask C.

p8c-poured.speaker: narrator
p8c-poured.text: The vicar takes Gerald a cup of cordial at every show. Gerald pours it on the roses.
p8c-poured.say: [dry, unhurried] The vicar takes Gerald a cup of cordial at every show. Gerald pours it on the roses.

p8c-rattled.speaker: narrator
p8c-rattled.text: The vicar, holding on to his bicycle when he saw the notebook.
p8c-rattled.say: [dry, unhurried] The vicar, holding on to his bicycle when he saw the notebook.

p8c-study.speaker: narrator
p8c-study.text: The vicar, alone in Gerald's study at four, looking in the drawers.
p8c-study.say: [dry, unhurried] The vicar, alone in Gerald's study at four, looking in the drawers.

p8c-syringe.speaker: narrator
p8c-syringe.text: Dilys and a syringe. Water, and only in marrows.
p8c-syringe.say: [dry, unhurried] Dilys and a syringe. Water, and only in marrows.

p8c-toby.speaker: narrator
p8c-toby.text: Gerald said the vicar couldn't add up. Twice this week.
p8c-toby.say: [dry, unhurried] Gerald said the vicar couldn't add up. Twice this week.

p8d-1.speaker: narrator
p8d-1.text: At the bar, between the darts team and the vet, the straw butcher has a pint in front of it. Nobody has drunk any.
p8d-1.say: [dry, unhurried] At the bar, between the darts team and the vet, the straw butcher has a pint in front of it. Nobody has drunk any.

p8d-2.speaker: quaile
p8d-2.text: Don't. It happens every year. Nobody owns up.
p8d-2.say: [weary] Don't. It happens every year. Nobody owns up.

p8e-1.speaker: narrator
p8e-1.text: The landlord comes over to talk about the quiz. Quaile turns her hearing aid off and smiles at him until he goes.
p8e-1.say: [dry, unhurried] The landlord comes over to talk about the quiz. Quaile turns her hearing aid off and smiles at him until he goes.

p8e-ask.speaker: quaile
p8e-ask.text: Gerald didn't drink that flask by himself. Somebody saw who handed it to him. Somebody always sees.
p8e-ask.say: [thoughtful] Gerald didn't drink that flask by himself. Somebody saw who handed it to him. [knowing] Somebody always sees.

p8e-good.speaker: quaile
p8e-good.text: I think you know, and I think you'd like me to say it. I shan't.
p8e-good.say: [smiling] I think you know, and I think you'd like me to say it. [beat] I shan't.

p8e-study.speaker: quaile
p8e-study.text: A chairman keeps notes. Nobody's read Gerald's.
p8e-study.say: [pointed] A chairman keeps notes. Nobody's read Gerald's.

p8e-vic.speaker: quaile
p8e-vic.text: Nobody's been to look at the vicar's garden. I'd have looked at the vicar's garden.
p8e-vic.say: [pointed] Nobody's been to look at the vicar's garden. I'd have looked at the vicar's garden.

p9-open.speaker: narrator
p9-open.text: The village hall. The prize-giving goes ahead, because Gerald would have wanted it, says the vicar, who is giving the prizes.
p9-open.say: [dry, unhurried] The village hall. The prize-giving goes ahead, because Gerald would have wanted it, says the vicar, who is giving the prizes.

p9a-1.speaker: clement
p9a-1.text: The Pike Cup for the heaviest marrow goes this year to Mrs Dilys Rudd.
p9a-1.say: [over-bright, into a microphone] The Pike Cup for the heaviest marrow goes this year to Mrs Dilys Rudd.

p9a-2.speaker: narrator
p9a-2.text: Dilys does not go up. One by one, the hall turns round to look at you.
p9a-2.say: [dry, unhurried] Dilys does not go up. One by one, the hall turns round to look at you.

p9b-1.speaker: narrator
p9b-1.text: Margaret in the front row, very upright. Dilys with her arms folded. Toby at the back, on his phone.
p9b-1.say: [dry, unhurried] Margaret in the front row, very upright. Dilys with her arms folded. Toby at the back, on his phone.

p9c-1.speaker: narrator
p9c-1.text: The vicar holds the cup with both hands. The lid rattles.
p9c-1.say: [dry, unhurried] The vicar holds the cup with both hands. The lid rattles.

p9e-argument.speaker: sam
p9e-argument.text: At one o'clock he showed you that notebook behind the produce tent. Then you fetched him a drink.
p9e-argument.say: [steady] At one o'clock he showed you that notebook behind the produce tent. Then you fetched him a drink.

p9e-flask.speaker: sam
p9e-flask.text: He died with one of your flasks by his chair.
p9e-flask.say: [quiet, final] He died with one of your flasks by his chair.

p9e-foxglove.speaker: sam
p9e-foxglove.text: Six foxgloves cut in your garden. Not slugs.
p9e-foxglove.say: [firm] Six foxgloves cut in your garden. Not slugs.

p9e-hall.speaker: narrator
p9e-hall.text: Forty people in the hall nod. They all bought cake.
p9e-hall.say: [dry, unhurried] Forty people in the hall nod. They all bought cake.

p9e-hunch.speaker: clement
p9e-hunch.text: I was on the cake stall all afternoon. Ask anyone.
p9e-hunch.say: [relieved, too loud] I was on the cake stall all afternoon. Ask anyone.

p9e-notebook.speaker: sam
p9e-notebook.text: The prize fund was four thousand short, and Gerald wrote it down: ask C, after the marrows.
p9e-notebook.say: [steady, clear] The prize fund was four thousand short, and Gerald wrote it down: ask C, after the marrows.

p9e-poured.speaker: sam
p9e-poured.text: He never drank your cordial. He poured it on the roses. So today you stayed and watched him drink it.
p9e-poured.say: [steady, pressing] He never drank your cordial. He poured it on the roses. So today you stayed and watched him drink it.

p9e-sit.speaker: quaile
p9e-sit.say: [quietly, tired] Sit down, Sam. Not tonight.

p9e-study.speaker: sam
p9e-study.text: And at four you were in his study, looking for the notebook.
p9e-study.say: [firm] And at four you were in his study, looking for the notebook.

p9f-dilys.speaker: dilys
p9f-dilys.text: I put water in marrows, love. Not in men.
p9f-dilys.say: [outraged, loud] I put water in marrows, love. Not in men.

p9f-margaret.speaker: margaret
p9f-margaret.text: I had forty-one foxgloves this morning, Sergeant. I still have forty-one. Count them.
p9f-margaret.say: [icy] I had forty-one foxgloves this morning, Sergeant. I still have forty-one. Count them.

p9f-toby.speaker: toby
p9f-toby.text: I was in a field with a man from Swindon. There's a video. It's very long.
p9f-toby.say: [offended, smug] I was in a field with a man from Swindon. There's a video. [beat] It's very long.

p9g-1.speaker: quaile
p9g-1.text: Sit down, Sam. Vicar, the prize fund is four thousand short, and your roof is not. Gerald was going to say so, after the marrows.
p9g-1.say: [firm, unhurried] Sit down, Sam. [beat] Vicar, the prize fund is four thousand short, and your roof is not. Gerald was going to say so, after the marrows.

p9g-3.speaker: narrator
p9g-3.text: The vicar clears his throat and gives Dilys Rudd the Pike Cup. Nobody claps.
p9g-3.say: [dry, unhurried] The vicar clears his throat and gives Dilys Rudd the Pike Cup. Nobody claps.

p9h-1.speaker: clement
p9h-1.text: He was going to stand up here and say it. In front of everyone. In front of the roof.
p9h-1.say: [breaking, fast] He was going to stand up here and say it. In front of everyone. [voice cracking] In front of the roof.

p9h-2.speaker: clement
p9h-2.text: I only wanted him to be ill. For the afternoon.
p9h-2.say: [small, ashamed] I only wanted him to be ill. For the afternoon.

p9h-3.speaker: quaile
p9h-3.text: The roof will still leak, Vicar.
p9h-3.say: [quiet, not unkind] The roof will still leak, Vicar.
